quote: All I wanted to do I'm an engineer, so I love reading about,
stewart_read: Customer explicitly states genuine interest in alternate energy technology — a real hook the rep could have used to re-engage instead of accepting the disqualification framing.
coaching_implication: Rep should have leaned into the engineer/technology interest to re-open curiosity rather than confirming disinterest at 00:42.

quote: so it sounds like you're not really looking at solar options for the home. Right?
stewart_read: Instead of the scripted small-ask ('can I have 30 seconds'), rep essentially invites the customer to confirm disinterest.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been trying to de-escalate the trickery complaint by giving the customer an easy out, which is a plausible de-escalation move but not schema-aligned.
coaching_implication: Use the hello_objection template — acknowledge, then ask for 30 seconds — instead of restating the objection as a closed question.

coaching_implication: Flip available: 'what's expensive is paying that same $150-200 with nothing to show after 25 years' — rep let it go unanswered entirely.

quote: And so you you can't put you can't put solar panels on a slate roof.

coaching_implication: Even in a likely-lost call, a quick 'have you gotten that confirmed by a specialist, slate roofs are sometimes workable' keeps the door open rather than an outright opt-out.
